_note: 6E Standard (400) skillsets — the profession half of a build. AUTHORED at ~50 points; the 5E sets
are 25, and that is a 250-point hero's skill list.
50 comes from the corpus: the five real 400-point 6E characters spend 30-69 on skills (median 59).
It is a NO-CSL budget and always was — four of those five carry no Combat Skill Levels at all, so
their 30-69 is already all real skills. Which matches Phil's rule: no CSLs at character creation,
because a CSL is a thing you must remember to apply and an OCV is just your OCV. The 5E
Investigator, Soldier and Warrior each carry one; none of these do.
A real 400-point character carries ~20 skills at 1-3 points each, not the 7-8 a 25-point set has.
So these are broad rather than deep: familiarities (1) and full skills (3), with the odd talent.
PROFESSION, not archetype. Any archetype can be a Soldier. Lightning Reflexes lives on the Warrior
for that reason — a Martial Artist gets it by being a Warrior, not by being a Martial Artist.
No cost is declared. The engine prices every skill; a set passes by totalling 50 when built.

skillsets.note:
Broad rather than deep, the way a real 400-point character's skills actually are: the 5E set's interactive core, plus the physical craft an actor has and the trade knowledge around it.

Charm, not Seduction — 6E deleted Seduction and folded it into Charm. KS, not AK — 6E has no generic Area Knowledge; an area is a Knowledge Skill.

Trading is a Proficiency (2) to close an odd remainder: Familiarity moves in 2s, so only the Proficiency lever can shave a single point. Same trick the 5E sets use.
Money is the perk; the rest is the room-reading a deal needs. The 5E set's seven, plus the paperwork and the polish.
The 5E set carried a Combat Skill Level; this one does not (see the no-CSL rule). Those points went into the legwork instead.
Two Science Skills, one of them the player's own. The 5E set's Skill Level is gone with the CSLs; the points bought breadth.
Money and the room. Charm rather than Seduction — 6E folded the two together.
The Fringe Benefit is the profession. KS: Home Country rather than AK — 6E has no generic Area Knowledge.

Three Science Skills, all the player's own. The legacy prose also lists 'Scientist', which is a skill ENHANCER rather than a skill — it discounts Science Skills — and it stays omitted here for the same reason the 5E set omits it.
The 5E set carried a Combat Skill Level; this one does not. A soldier's edge is the trade, not the level.
Cramming is the spy's whole trick: whatever the mission needs, learned on the flight over.
The 5E set's Skill Level went with the CSLs; this one is wider instead. It fixes things.

Lightning Reflexes lives here, and this is the only set that has it. It is a PROFESSION, so any archetype can be one — a Martial Artist gets First Strike by being a Warrior, not by being a Martial Artist. The 5E set's Combat Skill Level is gone; the trade replaced it.
